fills.reason: The app declares WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdk 28, minSdk 23) and QuickstartCredentialExporter writes the account's identity private keys, service password, profile key and account entropy pool as plaintext JSON to getExternalFilesDir(), which other apps with storage permission can read on API 23-28. It is reached from the internal settings screen but compiled into the release source set. SaveAttachmentUtil's public-directory writes are user-initiated media exports.

evidence.detail: Credential export targets app-specific external storage.
evidence.quote: val outputDir = context.getExternalFilesDir(null) ?: error("No external files directory")

evidence.detail: Private keys, service password and AEP are written unencrypted.
External storage write permission declared for API <= 28.

fills.reason: Looked at every SecretKeySpec construction for literal key bytes; all keys come from derived secrets, SecureRandom-generated material, the Android Keystore or protocol state (MasterSecret, attachment secret, backup keys, profile key). None is a hardcoded constant.

The release manifest enables backup with a key-value BackupAgent whose only item is SvrAuthTokens, so SVR2 authentication credentials are uploaded to and restored from Android Backup. This looks like an intentional choice so a PIN-based re-registration can skip SMS. The team should still confirm it accepts credentials in cloud backup.

evidence.detail: SVR2 auth tokens are serialized into the backup payload.

fills.reason: android:allowBackup is true in the release manifest and SignalBackupAgent backs up SvrAuthTokens (SVR2 credentials) to Android Backup. These are credentials, not excluded data. The demo/camera rules files the analyzer cited belong to a demo module that isn't shipped.

evidence.detail: SVR2 auth tokens are included in backup data.

fills.reason: Looked for logging of tokens, passwords, phone numbers and identifiers. Some log lines include E164/ACI values, but every Log call goes through AndroidLogger and PersistentLogger, which run Scrubber.scrub (email, UUID, PNI, phone and other patterns) before reaching logcat or the log file. Raw printStackTrace calls are only in image/video decoding code and log no user data.

Six WebViews enable JavaScript (recaptcha, captcha, PayPal, Stripe 3DS, debug log viewer), but none calls setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true), so the fail condition (all three settings) isn't met.
No WebView sets setAllowFileAccessFromFileURLs or setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs, and minSdk is 23 (>= 16), so both keep their secure default of false. The fail condition needs one of them true.
No addJavascriptInterface call or @JavascriptInterface method exists in the app or library sources, so no native bridge is exposed to WebView content.

Sensitive inputs use non-caching types: PIN entry uses NUMBER/TEXT_VARIATION_PASSWORD, passphrase fields use textPassword, registration lock uses numberPassword, payment recovery words use textVisiblePassword, and the backup key field uses KeyboardType.Password with autocorrect off.

Access codes are masked: PIN fields use password input types, passphrase fields use textPassword, and the Compose registration PIN uses PinVisualTransformation (bullet masking). The SMS verification code uses a custom VerificationCodeView showing digits, a common pattern a reviewer may still want to confirm.

FLAG_SECURE is applied unconditionally on PIN, backup/recovery key and payment card/bank screens (TemporaryScreenshotSecurity). Conversation screens are protected only when the user turns on Screen security, which defaults to false (TextSecurePreferences.java:543). Whether chats need protection by default is a product decision.

minSdk is 23 and notifications show sender name and message body by default (notification privacy default "all", TextSecurePreferences.java:438). The user can switch to name-only or no-name. Whether message content counts as sensitive data for this test is a product decision.

No overlay protection anywhere: no filterTouchesWhenObscured, onFilterTouchEventForSecurity, FLAG_WINDOW_IS_OBSCURED checks or setHideOverlayWindows, even on PIN, payment confirmation and device-linking screens.

evidence.detail: Registration lock PIN field has no touch filtering against overlays.

fills.reason: Searched for internal broadcasts and action-string intents. The internal broadcasts (SecurityEvent, KeyCachingService) call setPackage(own package) and require KEY_PERMISSION. No custom-action implicit activity or service intents were found.
The only internal broadcasts are package-scoped and permission-protected. No implicit intent carrying credentials or identifiers in extras to an unconstrained recipient was found.

minSdk is 23, and the shared PendingIntentFlags.mutable() helper returns FLAG_MUTABLE on API 31+ and 0 (mutable) below. It is used for dozens of notification content intents and alarms that don't need mutability. Base intents are mostly explicit, which reduces but doesn't remove the risk.

evidence.detail: Default helper makes PendingIntents mutable on every API level.
Notification content intent created mutable without need.

fills.reason: Every http/https deep-link intent-filter in the release manifest (signal.art, signal.group, signaldonations.org, signal.tube, signal.me, signal.link) sets android:autoVerify="true". Digital Asset Links verification itself wasn't checked.

Custom-scheme handlers validate their input. tsdevice/sgnl linkdevice ignores URI data and shows a confirmation dialog. sgnl addstickers hex-validates pack_id/pack_key. Group, proxy, signal.me, call-link and rereg links go through dedicated parsers (GroupInviteLinkUrl, SignalProxyUtil, SignalMeUtil, CallLinks) and confirmation dialogs.

java.util.Random, kotlin.random.Random and Math.random appear only for non-security uses: backup schedule jitter, backoff, UI colours, Compose previews, delay randomization and endpoint selection. Keys, IVs, tokens and IDs use SecureRandom.

Security values (master key, attachment secrets, idempotency keys, subscriber IDs, device-transfer nonces) come from SecureRandom. No time-based seeds or Calendar/Date-derived security values were found.
Cipher/KeyGenerator/SecretKeyFactory calls use AES (CTR, CBC, GCM) and a legacy PBE-AES key factory. No DES, 3DES, RC4 or Blowfish.
Every Cipher.getInstance transformation names CTR, CBC or GCM. No bare "AES" or ECB transformation. MasterSecretUtil line 317 uses the PBE...-CBC algorithm name.
The only KeyGenParameterSpec creates a symmetric AES key restricted to ENCRYPT|DECRYPT. No Keystore asymmetric key pair is generated with mixed purposes.

The only getInstance with a provider argument is KeyGenerator.getInstance(AES, "AndroidKeyStore") in KeyStoreHelper. The app installs its own Conscrypt/AesGcm providers via Security.insertProviderAt but doesn't name deprecated providers (BC, Crypto) in getInstance.

The legacy local encryption key (MasterSecret) is generated as AES-128. The Keystore wrapping key in KeyStoreHelper doesn't set a key size, so it also defaults to 128-bit AES. MASTG counts 128-bit AES as insufficient against quantum attacks.

evidence.detail: MasterSecret encryption key generated with a 128-bit AES key size.

fills.reason: The app checks for a secure lock screen via KeyguardManager.isDeviceSecure and isKeyguardSecure, and BiometricManager.canAuthenticate.

The shared BiometricDeviceAuthentication allows DEVICE_CREDENTIAL alongside biometrics. It gates screen lock, payment lock, payment confirmation, payments recovery phrase and device linking, so a device PIN is enough for those operations. MASTG treats this as a hardening weakness.

BiometricPrompt.authenticate is called without a CryptoObject, and no Keystore key uses setUserAuthenticationRequired(true). Success depends only on the callback, for screen lock, payment confirmation and device linking.

evidence.detail: Event-bound biometric prompt without a CryptoObject.

fills.reason: No call to setInvalidatedByBiometricEnrollment(false). The only KeyGenParameterSpec (KeyStoreHelper) doesn't touch it.

setConfirmationRequired(false) is set on the prompt that authorizes MobileCoin payments and the one that reveals the payments recovery phrase. Passive biometrics such as face unlock can then approve these without an explicit confirm tap.

evidence.detail: Payment confirmation prompt doesn't require explicit confirmation.
Recovery-phrase prompt doesn't require explicit confirmation.

fills.reason: No setUserAuthenticationParameters or setUserAuthenticationValidityDurationSeconds call. The only Keystore key isn't authentication-bound.

Tls12SocketFactory enables only TLSv1.2/1.3 on every SSLSocket, and the OkHttp ConnectionSpecs in SignalServiceNetworkAccess set tlsVersions(TLS_1_2). COMPATIBLE_TLS and explicit TLSv1/1.1 contexts aren't used.

"http://" literals in code are only in comments/Javadoc, a Linkifier display normalizer and scheme rewrites (https->wss, http->ws) on configured service URLs. No hardcoded http endpoint is used for requests, and the release build file has no http:// service URL.

TlsProxySocketFactory sets endpointIdentificationAlgorithm=HTTPS, and other TLS goes through OkHttp (which verifies hostnames). The device-transfer client (NetworkClientThread) opens an SSLSocket to a Wi-Fi Direct IP with no HostnameVerifier and authenticates the peer with a user-compared SAS code bound to the certificate. Whether that replaces hostname verification needs a reviewer's call.

BlacklistingTrustManager delegates to the platform/pinned trust manager and adds a serial blacklist (fine). SelfSignedIdentity.ApprovingTrustManager accepts any single server certificate in checkServerTrusted; DeviceTransferAuthentication then binds that certificate into an authentication code the user compares on both devices. Needs a reviewer to accept that SAS-based design.
No custom HostnameVerifier is implemented or set on any OkHttp client. ConscryptSignal only exposes wrapper APIs, and the proxy factory enables standard HTTPS endpoint identification.
None of the WebViewClients (recaptcha, captcha, PayPal, Stripe 3DS) overrides onReceivedSslError, so SSL errors keep the default cancel behaviour.

minSdk is 23 (< 24), so on Android 6 the default config trusts user-installed CAs. Signal's own service connections use dedicated TrustStores, which limits the impact; WebViews and third-party endpoints use the platform default.
The release manifests set no android:networkSecurityConfig, so no config adds <certificates src="user"/>. Only the nightlyStaging source set changes network config (usesCleartextTraffic).

ProviderInstaller.installIfNeeded is called only in censorship-circumvention mode and in AccountManagerFactory, not unconditionally before network use. The app instead bundles its own Conscrypt provider (inserted at position 2 in ApplicationContext). A reviewer should decide whether that meets the intent.

The release build type in app/build.gradle.kts doesn't set isDebuggable (default false). build-logic convention plugins contain no isDebuggable/debuggable setting, and no release manifest sets android:debuggable.
No call to WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled in app, feature or library sources.

The recaptcha/captcha WebViewClients intercept only the token scheme and otherwise allow any navigation. The PayPal client has no shouldOverrideUrlLoading, and Stripe 3DS sends non-web schemes out and allows the rest. 3DS and PayPal flows have to reach arbitrary bank domains, and no JS bridge or file access is exposed. Whether an allowlist is needed is a risk decision.
No EnableSafeBrowsing meta-data in the manifests and no setSafeBrowsingEnabled(false) or safeBrowsingEnabled = false in WebView code.
The repository has no native sources (no src/main/cpp or jni). Native libraries (libsignal, RingRTC, SQLCipher) come in prebuilt AARs, so PIC can only be checked on the built APK's .so files.
Native libraries come from prebuilt dependencies and there is no native source in the repo, so stack canaries need to be checked on the built APK's .so files.
The app checks Build.VERSION.SDK_INT in many places to switch to newer security APIs (e.g. biometric authenticators on API 30+, FLAG_MUTABLE on 31+).
This test needs a generated SBOM (CycloneDX) uploaded to Dependency-Track, including transitive dependencies. Ward's dependencies analyzer only covers direct dependencies under MASTG-TEST-0272.

getSerializableExtra/readSerializable are used only in non-exported components (RemoteReplyReceiver, DeviceToDeviceTransferService) or for in-app fragment results, with typed casts to app enums. Exported entry points (ShortcutLauncherActivity, DeepLinkEntryActivity) read only strings or URIs.
All four content providers (AvatarProvider, PartProvider, BlobContentProvider, FileProvider) are exported=false, and no provider uses appendWhere or concatenates URI path segments into SQL.

The app enforces updates: checkBuildExpiration runs at startup, and a server-driven isClientDeprecated flag disables message input (DisabledInputView 'this version has expired') and shows deprecated/outdated build banners.

Most security state lives in the SQLCipher database (per-page HMAC) via SignalStore. Some security toggles are still read from plain SharedPreferences (TextSecurePreferences, e.g. screen security) without an integrity check. Whether that matters depends on the attacker model (rooted device).
Release signing isn't configured in the repository (only the debug signingConfig at app/build.gradle.kts:169), so the signature schemes can only be checked on the signed release APK with apksigner.
The release signing key isn't in the repository, so the key size has to be checked on the signed APK with apksigner.
No StrictMode API references in app, core or lib main source sets.
Native binaries come from prebuilt dependencies and no native build config is in the repo, so debug symbols must be checked on the built APK's .so files.
No root detection anywhere in the app, core or lib sources (no su-binary, test-keys, RootBeer or Play Integrity checks), including at application startup.

evidence.detail: Application startup performs no root/environment integrity check.

fills.reason: The only debugger check (Debug.isDebuggerConnected in AnrDetector) suppresses ANR reports and triggers no security action. There is no JDWP or native anti-debugging.

evidence.detail: Debugger check used only for ANR reporting, not as a security control.

fills.reason: Release enables R8 (isMinifyEnabled = true), which renames identifiers only. Judging how hard the security logic is to reverse needs the decompiled APK, and the source is public anyway.
Native libraries are prebuilt dependencies, so native obfuscation has to be assessed by disassembling the packaged .so files.

No analytics or tracking SDK APIs (FirebaseAnalytics, Crashlytics, Sentry, Mixpanel, Amplitude, AppsFlyer, Adjust) are called. The manifest also turns off Firebase Analytics collection and ad-ID collection.
